'''Maxiron Agolerga''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Naboo (people)/Legends|native]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and the [[Pontifex/Legends|Pontifex]] of the [[Brotherhood of Cognizance/Legends|Brotherhood of Cognizance]]. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], he was approached by a woman who identified herself as "[[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Veré]]," who wished to be [[Marriage/Legends|married]] to a man identified as "[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Set]]." Agolerga agreed to perform the ceremony, and [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala/Legends|did so]] at [[Varykino/Legends|Varykino]], [[Lake Country/Legends|Lake Country]]. The young couple insisted that their union be kept a secret, and so Agolerga kept only limited records of it.

==Biography==
Maxiron Agolerga was the [[Pontifex/Legends|Pontifex]] of the [[Brotherhood of Cognizance/Legends|Brotherhood of Cognizance]], an arcane religious order of approximately twenty members that resided in [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo's]] mountains.<ref name="db" /> Agolerga counted among his friends the [[Naberrie family/Legends|Naberrie family]],<ref name="jvs">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> and in [[22 BBY]], he was approached by the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], who were presenting a private [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] message. Agolerga accepted the message, which contained an image of a [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|young woman]] who was requesting that he perform a secret [[Marriage/Legends|marriage]]. The Pontifex was surprised by the request, as no member of the Brotherhood had presided over a marriage for 300 years, since civil ceremonies had become popular during the reign of [[King/Legends|King]] [[Narmlé]].<ref name="db" />

Agolerga accepted the task, and donned his holy purple robes, before the two droids led him to a [[Gondola Speeder/Legends|Gondola Speeder]], and took him to [[Varykino/Legends|Varykino]], an estate on the other side of the [[Lake Country/Legends|Lake Country]]. There, the Pontifex met the young couple, who identified themselves as "Veré" and "[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Set]]," named for the fabled [[Veré]] and [[Set]], lovers in an old [[Futhork/Legends|Futhork]] legend. After a [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala/Legends|brief ceremony]], Agolerga pronounced the couple husband and wife. Before he departed Varykino, "Set" [[Mind trick/Legends|instructed]] the Pontifex not to tell anyone of their union, and so the only record Agolerga maintained of their matrimony was kept on a scroll in the Brotherhood's archives.<ref name="db" />

Agolerga later recorded the event once again, this time in a [[data book]]. When it was learned that the people he had wed were [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Padmé Amidala and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker, he passed the information onto Amidala's niece, [[Pooja Naberrie/Legends|Pooja Naberrie]].<ref name="jvs" /> The information, however, had not been kept as much of a secret as Agolerga thought, as both a member of the civil clergy<ref name="rotsn">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]] of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] had discovered it, and seen fit to inform [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who used the information to bend Skywalker to his will in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="rotsvd">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Despite the fact that he had been summoned to perform a wedding he knew nothing about, Agolerga was willing to take part in the ceremony. He was surprised that he, a member of a largely forgotten religion, was being tasked with marrying two people.<ref name="db" />

==Behind the scenes==
Maxiron Agolerga first appeared, as the "Naboo Holy Man," in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. In [[Matthew Stover]]'s [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], it is implied that a member of Naboo's civil clergy weds Skywalker and Amidala, which conflicted with the "holyman," identified in the various ''Attack of the Clones'' adaptations. The character was also identified as a holyman in ''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]'', ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', and ''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]''.

Through [[StarWars.com]]'s [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature ''[[What's The Story?]]'', [[Tim Veekhoven]], writing as "Sompeetalay," identified the character and elaborated upon his story. Since [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], which had identified the character as a friend of the Naberries, had been released after he had written the entry, but before it was published, Veekhoven was unable to reference it in his work. He derived the character's name from that of Manuel Aringarosa, a character from [[Wikipedia:Dan Brown|Dan Brown's]] [[Wikipedia:The Da Vinci Code|''The Da Vinci Code'']].<ref name="blog">{{Blog|teekay-421|13|They were the chosen ones}}</ref>
